### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35e7cae43d2805a73ad8ad8f61e0c249961c3136` — the merge of head `bb07931cb445ee6b0d4fc308b359dd87f9766d31` into base `c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35e7cae43d2805a73ad8ad8f61e0c249961c3136 && git checkout 35e7cae43d2805a73ad8ad8f61e0c249961c3136
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 bb07931cb445ee6b0d4fc308b359dd87f9766d31 && git checkout -B drift-repro c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 && git merge --no-ff bb07931cb445ee6b0d4fc308b359dd87f9766d31

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `064d4e01dc713cb2df6c30f60acf97c0a1cb6866`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts, packages/spec/src/data/projection-names-a-field.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`, `refuseEmptyListFilter`, the `?id=` / `?object=` steps of `createMetaListAnswer`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts and packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getMetaItems`, `readFlattenedMetaItems`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (the dispatcher's `getMetaItems` call), packages/client/src/index.ts (`meta.getItems`) — all read on `origin/main` `3d5933a9`, the merge base, as they stand

Inputs: card #29441 (body, 6582535222, 6592535841, 6592613238, 6594197602), ruling A on #29236 (6580261740), PR #29722 body, file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (5 files, +107/-0), and the head's check-runs. Not the dispatch order and not the dispatching seat's conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged against ruling A:

1. `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` gains an optional member `names` — **right.** The ruling's spec workload is exactly `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema.names`; the member is optional, so every request that parsed on `main` parses unchanged (widening only). Verified on the tree: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` ≈:264, between `packageId` and `previewDrafts`.
2. Element shape `z.string()`, no name grammar, no blank-member refusal — **right.** The ruling says an unknown name is simply absent, no 404; a member the schema judged would turn "absent" into "refused". It follows `searchFieldsArray()` (`z.array(z.string()).min(1, …)`, `search-fields-names-a-field.ts`), the sibling the ruling names for the spelling, rather than `transportProjectionArray` (which refuses a blank member with a regex): on the list door a blank name is a name that matches no item, which the ruling says is absent. `GetMetaItemRequestSchema.name` is a bare `z.string()` too.
3. `.min(1)` — an empty list refused at the schema, as a minimum, not a refinement — **right.** The ruling: "An empty value is refused `400` like `?id=`". `?id=` has no spec member (its refusal is the door's `refuseEmptyListFilter`, `meta-item-read-gate.ts` ≈:3497, step 3 of `createMetaListAnswer` ≈:3722), so it decides nothing about a list member; the spec siblings that ARE list members (`searchFieldsArray`, `transportProjectionArray`) both refuse `[]` for the reason the ruling gives (absent means "every item", so an empty filter read as absent is a widening). Published as `minItems: 1` in the JSON Schema, asserted by the test that calls `z.toJSONSchema` with `io: 'input'`; `authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/GetMetaItemsRequest:names` and no other shard moves. The 400 itself stays the door's, in the server PR, as the ruling orders.
4. Post-parse shape is a list, the wire is one comma-separated value split by the REST door — **right.** The ruling fixes the wire spelling to the data routes' comma convention; the list arity door (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`) refuses a repeated key, so the protocol member cannot be the wire's string and must be the split list. The test that refuses `'crm,helpdesk'` at the schema pins that the comma string is the door's, not the protocol's.
5. Push-down: the member sits on the request type `MetadataProtocol.getMetaItems(request: GetMetaItemsRequest)` consumes (`protocol.zod.ts` ≈:4455 on the head), so the server PR can carry it into `readFlattenedMetaItems` — **right**; the ruling names `GetMetaItemsRequest.names` as the push-down carrier.
6. `GetMetaItemsRequest['names']` is `string[] | undefined`, input and output alike — **right**; `Iso_api_protocol__GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` stays true, and the implementation class's inline parameter type `{ type; packageId?; previewDrafts? }` (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` ≈:3977) still accepts the widened request (an extra optional member is assignable), so nothing on `main` is broken by the widening.
7. No export added, removed or renamed; `api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/` unmoved — **right**, read off the diff: the schema and the type existed already.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29441-meta-items-names.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`; the PR body carries the same two lines at line start. **Matches what the diff publishes.** Measured against the gate and the precedents, not the body's account:

- The diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (one key, `api/GetMetaItemsRequest:names`). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (verdict table ≈:1876) refuses `Metadata-protocol: none` whenever an `authorable-surface/` shard moves (`none-baseline-moved`) and refuses `none` beside any `minor` entry (`none-minor`). The ruling's "spec minor" therefore cannot coexist with the card's `none`; the card's and the first claim's `none` was gate-impossible, and the seat amended the claim (6592613238) before the PR opened.
- `added` is the kind AGENTS.md assigns a newly accepted key, and `added` beside `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the gate's consistent pairing. Precedents verified on `origin/main`: #29521 (`45b4922d`, `.changeset/29373-export-withheld-maps.md`) and #29100 (`f1d795b1`, `.changeset/28914-package-export-bundle.md`) each moved the same `api.json` shard with one API key and declared `@objectstack/spec: minor` + `Clause-②: yes (widening)` + `Metadata-protocol: added`. This PR declares the same triple.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: success. The `Clause-②` arm is `(widening)`: no accept set narrows (every `main` request still parses), so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed.
- One carried note for the server seat (from the dev report's out-of-scope finding, confirmed against the gate): the ruling's server workload reads "rest / metadata-protocol / client minor" beside `Metadata-protocol: none`; the gate refuses that pairing (`none-minor`), so the server PR must declare a kind (`added`, by the same precedent) or ship `patch` entries. Escalated, not this PR's to fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6594197602 on #29441: `open_questions: []`; six `deviations`, one `out_of_scope_findings`, three acceptance notes in the PR body. Each answered:

- Deviation 1, `Metadata-protocol: added` against the card's and the ruling's `none` — **accepted**, gate-forced and precedent-backed (② above); the seat's amended claim 6592613238 is the record of agreement.
- Deviation 2, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on body and changeset while the claim spells bare `Clause-②: yes` — **accepted**; the same semver reading, and the ruled `(widening)` arm is the one the PR carries.
- Deviation 3, `pr_create` set the assignee `os-support-ai` and requested a reviewer — **accepted**; AGENTS.md says the PR's assignee mirrors the card's, set by the executor at `pr_create`; the harness line in `os-dev.md` yields to AGENTS.md.
- Deviation 4, the attribution line links the card thread, not the seat thread — **accepted**; the harness's required block, attribution only.
- Deviation 5, `origin/main` merged before opening, PR not subscribed — **accepted**; the merge keeps the net diff at the 5 files reviewed here; CI convergence is read below, not from a subscription.
- Deviation 6, `api-surface/` did not move — **accepted and verified** on the diff (no export change).
- Out-of-scope finding (server PR's `none` vs `minor`) — **escalated** to `domain:server#5` in ② above; not filed as a card, since it is a declaration the server PR's own gate will refuse at its first push.
- Acceptance note "declared before enforced" — **accepted with a should-fix** (④ item 1): the ruling orders the spec half first and the server PR is Blocked-by this card, so the lag is ruled, but the published describe says nothing of it.
- Acceptance note "blank segment `?names=a,,b` unruled" — **accepted**; the schema keeps `['']` (a name matching no item, absent by the ruling), and whether the door trims or refuses a blank segment is the server PR's to decide and teach; the schema's `.min(1)` backs either choice (a door that drops blanks and arrives at `[]` meets the ruled empty refusal).
- Acceptance note on #29415 (same file, different region) — **accepted**; ordinary concurrency, the later lander regenerates.
- Card-level: the dispatch tier line in the claim (`model: TIER_DEFAULT`) governs the executor; this record is the contract-tier review the schema face owes, served here.

Gate verdicts, read off the head's check-runs at 2026-11-03T03:03Z: 33 success, 8 skipped (the path-filtered UI and opt-in jobs), 0 failure. Every gate-carrying job that had concluded is green — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Live E2E UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `(6/8)`, `(8/8)`. Still in progress at that reading: `Test Core` shards 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, `Test UI` 15 of 16 shards and `Type Check UI`. ⛔ This record is posted only once those conclude `success`; a `failure` among them voids the PASS below and the record is re-rendered, not posted.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` only (tests, `api.json`, `protocol.mdx` and the changeset read, not reviewed).

Against ruling A: only the named items are answered ("among those the list would answer without it" keeps the per-caller gate and `packageId` ahead of the narrowing, where the ruling puts the step); an unknown name is absent, no 404 (no member is judged); an empty value is refused rather than read as every item (`.min(1)`, with the door's 400 named as the wire's answer); the push-down carrier is `GetMetaItemsRequest.names`. All four hold on the tree. Usable by the first consumer: the server PR reads `query.names` once at the list door (one more name in `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`'s closed set), splits it, refuses `''` before building the request as `?id=` is refused, and passes `names` through `getMetaItems` into `readFlattenedMetaItems`; `meta.getItems(type, { names })` serialises `names.join(',')`, and the client's `[]` becomes the door's `?names=`, refused with 400, the same answer the schema gives — the two layers agree. The describe is a rule only: no tracker number in the describe or in the `.min` message; the docblock's citations (`#29236`, record 6580261740) sit in TSDoc beside the file's existing ruling citations, not in a runtime string. The docblock's cross-references were read and are accurate: `searchFieldsArray` at `../data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts`, `refuseEmptyListFilter` in `@objectstack/rest`, the list door's repeated-key arity rule.

Tried to break it:

- `names` beside `packageId`: both narrow, order-independent, no conflict. `names` beside `previewDrafts`: the ruling places the narrowing after the gate, so a draft-overlaid item named in `names` is answered as the overlay answers it; nothing in the schema contradicts that.
- `['crm', 'crm']` accepted: a duplicate name narrows to the same item once; the answer shape is unchanged. Not a defect.
- `.min(1)` before `.optional()`: the right order; `undefined` stays accepted, `[]` refused with one `too_small` at `['names']`.
- A caller on today's runtime sending `names`: `getMetaItems` ignores it and the full list is answered (`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` ≈:54 reads only `type`, `packageId`, `previewDrafts`; the dispatcher calls `protocol.getMetaItems({ type })`). This is the ruled interim, declared in the changeset — but not in the describe (item 1 below).

Findings:

1. **should-fix** — the describe is published to `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` as a served capability while no door reads `names` until the server PR on #29236 lands. The file's own precedent for a member declared ahead of its runtime is a `[PLANNED — not yet served]` opener on the describe (the device-registration schemas in this file, ≈:3587 on the head; #29521 and #29100, the two precedents this PR cites for its declarations, both carried it), removed by the PR that serves it. The changeset says it; the published reference row does not. Prime Directive #10 ("never advertise a capability the runtime doesn't deliver") is the rule; the ruling's ordered two-PR shape and the Blocked-by chain bound the window, which is why this is should-fix, not must-fix. Either prefix the describe now, or have the server PR's seat accept that its PR is the one that makes the published row true and land it before any version pass.
2. **note, no fix** — the describe mentions the HTTP status (`400`) a spec schema cannot itself answer; precedent in the same schema family (`GetMetaItemRequestSchema.member`: "Refused with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`") makes this the file's convention, and the ruling's own words are "refused `400`".

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb07931cb445ee6b0d4fc308b359dd87f9766d31`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts (the proxy the new pin reads `.shape` through), packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts and packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (the `/meta/:type` list door, which has no closed query set on `main`), packages/rest/src/query-allowlist.ts (`refuseUnknownQueryParams`, mounted on the item-history, crud and write doors only), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts (`getMetaItems`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (the dispatcher's list read) — read on `origin/main` `3d5933a9` as they stand

Delta review: two commits on top of the reviewed head `064d4e01` — `8b17a599` (src + test) and `bb07931c` (regenerated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`); `git diff 064d4e01..bb07931c` is 3 files, +20/−6. The changeset, `authorable-surface/api.json` and every judgment of the record on `064d4e01` that the delta does not touch carry over unchanged; this record re-judges only what moved and re-reads the gates on the new head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set unchanged — **right.** The delta edits a describe string, a TSDoc paragraph and one test; `names` keeps `z.array(z.string()).min(1).optional()`, `minItems: 1` and `string[] | undefined`. No shard other than the generated reference row moves, so no declaration line moves.
2. The describe now opens `[PLANNED — not yet served] ` — **right, and true against the code today.** No list door reads `names`: `getMetaItems` (`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts:54`) reads only `type`, `packageId`, `previewDrafts`; the dispatcher calls `protocol.getMetaItems({ type })`; `meta.getItems` in the client sets only `package`. The marker is the file's convention for a member declared ahead of its producer (the device-registration schemas, #29521, #29100), which the record on `064d4e01` named as its should-fix.
3. The new closing sentence "No list door reads it yet: until one does, a request carrying it is answered as if it were absent." — **true against the code today.** `refuseUnknownQueryParams` is mounted on the item-history, crud and write doors, not on the `/meta/:type` list (`meta-collection-routes.ts` refuses only an unknown list TYPE, `refuseUnknownMetaListType`); the ruling itself says the closed set `(package, preview, object, include, id, names)` is the server PR's. So `?names=a,b` on `main` is neither read nor refused and the full list is answered: "as if it were absent" is exactly the behaviour. It is also true for a protocol-level call carrying `names`, which `getMetaItems` ignores.
4. Published reference row regenerated — **right**; the `protocol.mdx` row is byte-equal to the describe's concatenation, and only that row moved.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the record on `064d4e01`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, matching the diff (the `api.json` shard still moves by the one key and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` still refuses `none`). A describe edit changes no accept set and no kind. `Check Changeset` on `bb07931c` is read below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The prior record's **should-fix 1 is resolved**: the published row now says the member is not served and what a request carrying it gets until it is. No must-fix existed.
- The dev's account of the delta (marker added, closing sentence, docblock paragraph, one new pin, changeset untouched, gen:docs moved only `protocol.mdx`) matches the tree — judged on the diff, not the account.
- New obligation on the server seat, **carried, not a fix here**: the docblock promises "the server PR on #29236 drops the marker in the change that serves the member", and the new pin (`protocol.test.ts` ≈:1933) makes that a red test until it does. That puts one `packages/spec` edit (describe + pin removal + gen:docs) into the server PR's file surface, which the ruling's server workload lists as rest / runtime / metadata-protocol / client only. The server seat's claim must name it; the alternative — a spec PR of its own to drop the marker — would leave the published row stale for one lap. Escalated to `domain:server#5` with the `none`-vs-`minor` declaration note already carried from the prior record.
- The docblock paragraph carries `#29236` in TSDoc, not in a runtime string; the pin itself asserts the describe carries no tracker id (`/#\d{3,}/`), and the describe's `400` / `404` are status codes with no `#`, so the pin is satisfiable and is.
- Check-runs on the superseded head `064d4e01` were cancelled mid-run by the push (`Test Core (3/8)` concluded `cancelled` at 03:12Z); that head is no longer the PR's and its record is not posted.

Gate verdicts on `bb07931c`, every check-run complete: 57 success, 8 skipped (path filters and opt-in lanes), 0 failure or cancelled. The PASS below stands on a green head.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` only. The member still holds against ruling A exactly as judged on `064d4e01` (named items only, unknown name absent, empty refused, push-down carrier `GetMetaItemsRequest.names`); the delta adds no behaviour. The marker sentence and the closing sentence are both statements about today's runtime and both are true (① 2–3). The describe stays a rule plus a served-state statement, with no tracker number. Usable by the first consumer: the server PR removes a fixed prefix and a trailing sentence and deletes one `it(...)`; nothing else in the member changes under it.

Tried to break it: the new pin reads `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema.shape.names.description` through `lazySchema`'s proxy, whose `get` trap forwards every non-`_zod` property to the resolved real schema (`lazy-schema.ts` ≈:125), and `.describe()` on the `.optional()` wrapper sets that wrapper's `description`, so the read answers the describe (same shape as `EvalUserSchema.shape.isPlatformAdmin.description` in `identity/eval-user.test.ts`). Under `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS=1` the real object is returned and the read is the same. The marker regex requires one space after `]`, which the describe has. No finding.

Findings: none. No must-fix, no should-fix.
